Want to plant a garden? Get seeds and advice from the Example Garden Club. Apply here.

The first thing to understand about gardens is that they are slow. A gardener who expects results in a week has mistaken the work for something else, and the mistake costs a season.

Soil is the second thing. Most of what a plant needs is not in the seed but in the ground around it, and a patient person can improve ground for years with nothing more than compost, rain and time.

Finally there is the matter of attention. A garden left alone does not stay as it was; it becomes something else. Looking at it every day is how a gardener learns what it is becoming.

None of this is complicated, and none of it is quick. That is the whole essay, and the rest of this page repeats it in more words so that the text cell is plainly the longest thing here.
